title: Phasor: exact holograms for .NET
description: Phasor is a .NET library whose Pleroma stores items in one fixed array and answers key, flag, order and time questions exactly, refusing past capacity.
headline: One exact hologram, many views.
intro: Phasor's main object is the Pleroma. An item is a key plus, optionally, a flag word of up to 16 bits, an arrangement of up to 5 things and a tick on a clock. One array of finite-field harmonics answers exact counts per key and whole items (refusing past the key capacity), exact counts per flag word, how many items lie within r bits of a query and which stored words are nearest, counts per arrangement, counts per tick, and opt-in joint counts over flags, order and time. Everything except the key views stays exact at any load.

The whole store relabels, shifts keys, ages and diffuses over time in place with every view still exact, and a weighted superposition of flips, relabellings and time shifts applies to the whole store in one pass. Under the Pleroma is the phasor codec, a vector symbolic codec that encodes numbers and symbols as unit-complex faces and composes them with bind, unbind, bundle and correlate.

why.title: Exact where others approximate
why.text: At equal storage, the exact key view recovered 64 items with no errors where Plate's holographic reduced representations held 95% or better only up to 4. Past capacity it refuses, where the baseline answers wrongly every time.

why.title: One array, many questions
why.text: Counts per key, flag word, arrangement and tick, nearness, joint counts and any predicate are read from slices of one array, so adding a view does not add a second store.

why.title: Whole-store operations in one pass
why.text: A weighted superposition of flips, relabellings and time shifts applies to every item at once, at a cost that does not depend on how many elements the kernel holds.

diagram.title: The map
diagram.stageLabel: Interactive 3D pyramid of the Pleroma operation grid. Drag to turn it. Use the arrow keys to move between cells.
diagram.lede: The Pleroma's operations as a pyramid: three faces, eight rungs and a lid, {cells} cells in all. Each cell is a public member with its status, API and evidence. Turn it, select a cell, or colour it by status.

quickstart.lede: Build a store of items, read it back exactly, then age it.

capabilities.title: Views of one store
capabilities.text: TryKeys and TryItems for exact counts per key and whole items, Flags, Near and Nearest for flag words and closeness, Arrangements and SignBalance for order, Times for ticks, and JointCounts over any set of faces.

capabilities.title: Any predicate, one read
capabilities.text: CountWhere counts the items whose flag word satisfies any predicate, linear or not, exactly and at any load, with one inner product. Attend returns exact counts, shares and parity from one read.

capabilities.title: Whole-store operations
capabilities.text: Tick and Diffuse age every item, RelabelFlags, RelabelArrangements and ShiftKeys relabel the store without reading items back, and a PleromaKernel applies a weighted sum of such moves in one pass.

capabilities.title: Bind two stores
capabilities.text: Bind adds keys, XORs flags, composes arrangements and adds ticks for every pair of items at once. Binding with a one-item store shifts the whole store on every face together.

capabilities.title: Pages, sparse and dense
capabilities.text: A dense page reads every one of up to 4,096 slots exactly in one transform, and joins two pages exactly in one read. A sparse page holds exact counts over a huge key set in memory proportional to the keys present.

capabilities.title: Redundancy and repair
capabilities.text: Reserved keys detect and repair lost harmonics, a mirror in a second prime detects corruption in either copy, and an exact-sum parity rebuilds any one lost store.

capabilities.title: Keys only
capabilities.text: CycleHologram is the Pleroma with keys only. It returns every stored symbol and count exactly up to its capacity, refuses past it, and adds and subtracts exactly, so two replicas can find what differs by exchanging one small hologram.

capabilities.title: The phasor codec
capabilities.text: PhasorCodec, HoloCodec and Hologram encode numbers and symbols as faces and compose them with bind, unbind, bundle and correlate. One operator set works on numbers, text and their mixtures.

limits: There is no key-addressed attention. The key view returns exact whole items up to capacity. It is not a similarity search on keys.
A store of key capacity K holds 2K+1 harmonics per key line and decodes up to K distinct keys. Past that it refuses.
Counts must stay within the field's range. On a small prime field, weighted queries scale counts by the weight, so keep totals times the weight below half the field.
The Pleroma runs on the CPU. There is no GPU kernel.
It is a data structure and a set of operations, not a trainable embedding engine. The continuous phasor bundle is the approximate store; the Pleroma is the exact one.

Exact arithmetic is not faster in general. A Pleroma read costs one or more transforms, while a float bundle read is one correlation. At equal bits float reads are often faster, and at large loads the two converge.
The two codec layouts do not mix. Hologram and PhasorCodec use the interleaved layout, HoloCodec the planar one.
PhasorCodec needs an even dimension of at least 128.
reference: Every public type is documented with a worked example in the package readme on NuGet.
